- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate early in horizon; reduce initial forecast peaks.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates downward moves; increase early forecast lows.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), especially in 30-day horizon — cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 2x recent mean.
- If sentiment shows strong mean-reversion (e.g., 0.00 then 0.67), model fails to adjust — force forecast to align with sentiment trend reversal.
- For long horizons (e.g., 30d), model overreacts to recent spikes; apply exponential decay to recent sentiment to smooth forecast.
- If true outcome shows rapid divergence from history (e.g., >2x standard deviation), reduce forecast volatility — especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is stable (e.g., 0.50–0.67 for 5+ days), model should not overfit to short-term noise — use 3–5 day moving average of history for baseline.
